status: Before final or finite runs; pilot results are exploratory
purpose: Retain same-policy server controls and each server one-shot control, so client and server effects are identifiable. Index candidate subject to pilot and safety validation before freeze.

aggregation.deadline: same-sized measure cohorts; mean rate and individual repeats
aggregation.latency: Report each repeat; adoption p99 uses pooled raw eligible successful-purchase/expired-reservation durations across three repeats, never average p99 mislabeled pooled
aggregation.cpu: sum whole-host CPU seconds / sum internal purchases in exactly matching individual observation windows; report per-run variation and absolute CPU
aggregation.paired: same seed/rate logical index; count gained/lost with per-repeat variation, not proof individual counterfactual under identical runtime scheduling

finite.rationale: At 400/s and mixed actions, cancellation returns some stock immediately, while paid/expiry holds consume initial stock before the 15s expiry wave. Continued unique demand tests returned-stock allocation. The stock cap is a real outcome ceiling, not server throughput capacity.
finite.requirement: Observe sold-out responses and stock exhaustion during continuing demand; if absent, preserve run and explicitly declare a new diagnostic condition instead of pretending depletion occurred. Same conditions for all arms.
finite.attribution: Per-bucket allocation and return commit observations plus actual DB original_bucket_id. Units are fungible: allocation beyond the initial quota is return-backed accounting; do not assert physical unit identity. Show TTL->return->subsequent allocation->purchase chronology and whole user outcomes; causal purchase improvement is paired same-demand difference, not reuse count alone.

additional_common_observation: Before final freeze, same afterCommit allocation timestamp and 1s inventory snapshots on every compared source. AfterCommit logs are observations that may be lost on process failure; independent DB+PG audit remains authority. Callback timestamps are not a serialization clock.
